description:
## The defect

`/reviewer` **is** the queue. "Enter as reviewer" from the landing page drops a
human straight onto submission #1 with the scorecard already open — no page that
says who they are, what they are responsible for, how much is left, when it
closes, or where their own record lives. "Exit queue" is `window.history.back()`,
which from a freshly opened seat means nowhere.

Every other seat has a home. The organizer has `/dashboard`; the speaker has
`/portal` with tasks, profile and talks. The reviewer has a work surface and no
seat. That is the gap.

Operator ruling, 2026-08-13: split the seat in two.

- **`/reviewer`** — the reviewer's home. Who you are, what you're responsible
  for, what you've done, and one way in.
- **`/reviewer/queue`** — the working surface. One submission, one
  recommendation, next.

## What the home page is

Four blocks, in this order. Every number on it already has data behind it —
nothing here needs a new source of truth.

**1 · Your assignment.** Plan and round name, mode (Scorecard / Comparison),
anonymity ("Anonymous review" / "Identity visible"), `N waiting · M reviewed of
T`, and the round's `closes_at` as a plain date when one is set (schema:
`evaluation_rounds.closes_at`, nullable — say nothing rather than invent a
deadline). Primary action **Start reviewing →** goes to `/reviewer/queue` and
resumes at the next unreviewed item. When the queue is clear the card says so and
the primary action becomes a quiet secondary — an empty queue is a finished job,
not an error.

**2 · Your responsibility.** The track scopes already returned as `scopes`, the
committee(s) this reviewer sits on, and the existing one-sentence rule ("A
submission appears when it is assigned to you — directly or through your
committee — and carries a track in your scope."). Committee membership is *not*
in the queue payload today; add it there rather than minting a second endpoint.
No scope assigned is a real state and must read as one — a reviewer with an empty
queue deserves to know whether nobody assigned them work or nobody gave them a
track.

**3 · Your reviews.** The `completed` list that lives under the queue today,
moved here whole: title, the recommendation recorded (or "Conflict"), and Reopen
→ the same detail modal. Keep `completed_truncated`'s honest caption.

**4 · Your profile.** Name, email, title, company, bio, headshot, editable
inline. **No new API** — `PATCH /api/v1/me/profile`
(`src/routes/portal.routes.ts:1454`) is `auth: { kind: "authenticated" }`, not
speaker-gated, and `ProfileForm` in `src/ui/portal/PortalPage.tsx` already does
this work. Reuse it or lift it into a shared component; do not fork a second
profile editor. If the operationId or copy says "speaker" in a way a reviewer
would find odd on screen, fix the copy, not the route.

## What the queue becomes

Keeps: the submission card, the scorecard (recommendation, optional score,
criteria, committee note), Declare conflict, the A/M/D · 1–5 · Enter shortcuts,
the full-submission modal, comparison mode.

Sheds: the responsibility panel and the Completed list — both now live on home,
and leaving copies here makes "Completed" mean two different things depending on
which page you are standing on.

Gains: an honest progress line (`17 of 40`) in the topline, and **Exit queue
becomes a real link to `/reviewer`**, not `history.back()`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `/reviewer` renders the home with all four blocks. It does not render a
   scorecard.
2. `/reviewer/queue` renders the working surface, unchanged in its scoring
   behaviour, and every existing reviewer AC still passes against it.
3. **Start reviewing** lands on the first unreviewed assigned submission.
4. **Exit queue** returns to `/reviewer` from a cold-opened tab (no history).
5. Saving a recommendation on the queue and then returning home shows that
   submission under Your reviews with the recommendation that was saved.
6. Editing bio/title/company/headshot on home persists and survives a reload,
   through the existing `/me/profile` route, with no new endpoint added.
7. A reviewer with zero track scopes sees a home that says so; a reviewer with an
   empty queue sees a finished-work state, not an error.
8. Anonymity is unchanged. Blind mode still redacts identity everywhere it does
   today, and the home page must not leak a submitter's name through the
   completed list.
9. Mobile: home is usable at 375px (the queue already carries
   `data-mobile-review`).

## Known touchpoints — check every one

- `src/ui/review/ReviewerPage.tsx`, `src/ui/review/review.css`
- `src/ui/shell/route-table.ts:55` — the `reviewer` route entry
- `src/ui/shell/AppShell.tsx:127,173` — `/reviewer` is special-cased twice as a
  non-admin shell; `/reviewer/queue` needs the same treatment
- `src/lib/auth/signin-destination.ts:18` — reviewer sign-in destination
- `src/routes/signin.route.tsx:159` — the demo reviewer button's `data-signin-to`
- `src/routes/landing.route.tsx:191` — "Enter as reviewer"
- `src/ui/shell/seat.tsx:58` — "Open your review queue"
- `src/routes/evaluation.routes.ts:954` — the committee-invite magic link mints
  `redirectTo: "/reviewer"`. An invited reviewer should land on their home, which
  is now the right answer rather than an accident.
- `public/submission/index.html` — three hardcoded
  `marquee.stage11.dev/reviewer?demo=reviewer` links
- `scripts/checks/speed.ts:140` — loads `/reviewer` and waits for
  `[data-reviewer-surface]`. Decide deliberately whether the speed check measures
  home or queue, and make it measure the one that matters (the queue is the
  latency that hurts a reviewer). Do not let this silently start timing a
  lighter page and report a false win.
- `docs/ROUTES.md:43,101` and `SITEMAP.md` — both list `/reviewer` as "Review
  queue"
- `cli/marquee.mjs` and `SKILL.md` — CLI reviewer verbs hit the API, not the
  route, so they should need no change; confirm rather than assume.
- Tests keying on the reviewer surface, at least:
  `tests/node/reviewer-boundary.AC-214-246.test.mjs`,
  `tests/node/reviewer-anonymity.AC-64.test.mjs`,
  `tests/node/eval-dead-ends.test.mjs`,
  `tests/unit/signin-destination.MRQ-133.test.ts`,
  `tests/integration/signin.MRQ-133.test.ts`,
  `tests/integration/landing.test.ts`, and `scripts/checks/check-routes.mjs`.

## Do not

- Do not add a second profile endpoint, a second queue endpoint, or a second
  reviewer identity concept.
- Do not put organizer chrome (the admin sidebar) on either reviewer page. The
  reviewer seat has its own topline for a reason.
- Do not show a reviewer the round's aggregate score distribution or the
  committee's Approve/Maybe/Deny split. It was considered and left out
  deliberately: showing a reviewer how everyone else is voting nudges their next
  vote.
- Do not leave a duplicated Completed list on the queue.

## Validation

Green tests are not the gate. Drive the real thing: sign in through the demo
reviewer door, land on home, read the numbers, start reviewing, save a
recommendation, exit back to home, confirm the review appears with the
recommendation you gave, edit the profile, reload, confirm it stuck. Use the c11
embedded browser (WKWebView — run local dev with
`--var INSECURE_LOCAL_COOKIES:1` or the session cookie is dropped on `http://`).
Screenshots of home and queue in the PR.
title: The reviewer seat has no home — /reviewer drops you onto a scorecard
